method: Each section read in full by a machine-assisted reviewer against the packs and the ground catalogue as of this date; not a legal review.

sections.bearsOn: Defines for the Act and its regulations the terms the practice rules turn on: Coast (the former Coast Forest Region) and Interior (the rest of BC), fish stream (frequented by a listed species, or under 20% gradient over each 100 m unless an inventory or a proven barrier shows otherwise), the specified species of fish, licensed waterworks intake (a municipal, regional or improvement district waterworks licence, or a water users' community's domestic licence), stream, road (its pit, quarry and landing in the clearing width included), excavated or bladed trail, and operating season.
sections.gapNote: The private managed forest land pack uses Coast and Interior for the reforestation densities; whether a stream is a fish stream, and so classed, is the reviewer's answer and its 20% gradient test is not asked.

sections.bearsOn: The wildlife minister may set water quality objectives for a stream upstream of a licensed waterworks intake, after consulting affected owners, effective six months after the council is told; the minister may enter to monitor on 14 days' notice.
sections.gapNote: A rule would ask whether a water quality objective is set for a stream above an intake that the block drains to, which Council Regulation s. 24(3)(b) then reads for fertilizer.

sections.bearsOn: The council need not consider a review request about the annual administration fee or the exit fee's calculation.
Sets the form of an owner's notice taking on a remediation order.
Contravening the Council Regulation's practice sections (13–24, 27–30) is an offence with a fine of up to $500,000, and its notice and selection sections up to $25,000.
